facts.text: Erzsébetváros became an independent district in 1873 after Budapest's unification and was named in 1882 after Queen Elisabeth, reflecting a desire for prestige.
The district's core was the historic Jewish Quarter, bounded by Király utca, Dohány utca, and Károly körút, a center of Jewish life until WWII.
In 1894 the New York Coffee House opened on Erzsébetváros, quickly turning into a hub for artists and writers with marble interiors and painted ceilings.
The area began to be parceled and populated in the early 18th century after the Turkish occupation, with streets like Király and Dob emerging.
